events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** My expected boat rating for this week is **3 (good)**.
- **Fish 85-150 ft of water, with lines about 50-90 ft down.** Run blue or green spoons and a white flasher-fly combo.
- **Backups:** St. Joseph and South Haven, each about **2 (average)**. Run 90-130 ft with glow spoons or flasher-flies.
- **Muskegon:** I'd expect **1 (below average)**. Skip it unless conditions change.
- **Skip the piers** for now.

## Why

- **Grand Haven ranks highest because its latest boat report was good.** The Aug 12 report rated boats 3 and named the depths and lures above.
- **St. Joseph and South Haven sit a step lower.** Their Aug 12 boat reports show fish present at 55-90 ft down, but St. Joseph was not rated and South Haven was rated average.
- **Muskegon ranks lowest because its latest report was slow.** The Aug 12 report says anglers were unsuccessful because of warm water.
- **Piers are a poor bet right now.** The Aug 12 Grand Haven report says warm water stopped pier salmon catches.
- **I'd expect the offshore boat bite to hold for now.** Buoy water at all four ports was about 72-74 F and rose only about 1 F over the past week, so there was no sign of cooling that would move fish toward the piers.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest are Aug 12, all from the same bulletin):**
- Grand Haven (2026-08-12): boat, quality 3 (good). "Salmon were caught 50 to 90 feet down in 85 to 150 feet of water… Blue and green spoons worked well, along with a white flasher-fly combo." Pier: quality 0 (slow), "Due to increasing water temperatures, no salmon or steelhead were reported from the pier."
- South Haven (2026-08-12): boat, quality 2 (average). "A fair number of salmon were reported 45 to 90 feet down in 100 to 130 feet of water… Green or blue glow spoons worked well."
- St. Joseph (2026-08-12): boat, not rated. "Boat anglers found salmon along with a few steelhead 55 to 80 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water… White flasher-fly combinations and glow spoons produced the most bites."
- Muskegon (2026-08-12): boat, quality 0 (slow). "Anglers targeting salmon were unsuccessful due to warm water," though it noted glow spoons and plugs in low light.
- Reports from July 22 (Grand Haven boat quality 3, Muskegon boat quality 2) are older and show a cooler lake, so I weighted them less.

**Past seasons (history, buoy water about 71-73 F, mid-August):**
- Grand Haven was good in several years, including 2025-08-20 (quality 3: "50 to 100 feet down in 80 to 220 feet of water") and 2024-08-07 (quality 3: "35 to 90 feet down in 70 to 230 feet of water").
- Results at the other ports were mixed. South Haven and St. Joseph were slow in some years (2025-08-13, 2025-08-20, 2023-08-23) and good in others (2024-08-07 St. Joseph, quality 4; 2024-08-28 South Haven, quality 3).
- I'd expect fish to stay spread out and deeper water to pay in warm weeks like these, as past reports often describe.

**Conditions now:**
- Buoy surface water was 74 F at St. Joseph, 73 F at South Haven, and 72 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, each up about 1 F over the week. This is the summary for the week before Aug 18, not live data.
- No wind forecast or modeled cold-layer depth was available in this session.

## Caveats

- **The newest report is from Aug 12, six days old.** Treat these ratings as a guide to the week, and check the next bulletin before you go.
- **Water temperatures are measured at offshore buoys, not at the piers.** Live readings and the cold-layer depth were not available, so I could not confirm whether cooler water is moving in.
- **Check the wind before going out.** I have no wind forecast here. Small boats should check conditions before heading out on this big lake.
- **St. Joseph's rating is an estimate.** Its only recent report was not rated, so I treated it as a weak positive.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, Aug 12 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/424a154
- Past-season bulletins cited for history: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3eeac7b (Aug 20, 2025), https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3ad6654 (Aug 7, 2024), https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b19036 (Aug 28, 2024)
